title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZQ (Provisions of this Chapter to override other laws)

content.overview: Section 378ZQ gives Chapter XXIA effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent with it in the Companies Act, another law in force, or an instrument having effect under such a law. Provisions of another Act, law or instrument continue to apply to a Producer Company to the extent they are not varied by, or inconsistent with, Chapter XXIA.
content.glance: Chapter XXIA prevails over inconsistent provisions, while non-varied and non-inconsistent provisions of other laws or instruments continue to apply.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZQ (Provisions of this Chapter to override other laws). Chapter XXIA has effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent with it in the Companies Act, any other law in force, or an instrument having effect by virtue of such a law. The section preserves the application of other laws or instruments insofar as they are not varied by, or inconsistent with, Chapter XXIA. It is therefore not a blanket displacement of all other law. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Priority for inconsistent provisions
sections.body: Chapter XXIA has effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent with it in the Companies Act, any other law for the time being in force, or an instrument having effect by virtue of such a law.

sections.heading: Other provisions continue where consistent
sections.body: Other Acts, laws and instruments continue to apply to a Producer Company insofar as they are not varied by, or inconsistent with, the provisions of Chapter XXIA.

sections.heading: Application method
sections.body: Identify the relevant Chapter XXIA provision and the competing provision or instrument, then explain the actual inconsistency or variation. Do not assert that a whole enactment is displaced when only a particular provision conflicts.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZQ: Provisions of this Chapter to override other laws

examples.title: Testing an asserted conflict
examples.body: Where a party relies on another statutory provision in relation to a Producer Company, identify the relevant Chapter XXIA rule and the precise inconsistency, if any. If no variation or inconsistency is established, section 378ZQ preserves the application of the other provision to the extent stated in the section.

hypotheticals.question: A party argues that section 378ZQ excludes an entire other statute from applying to a Producer Company. What should be checked?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify the exact Chapter XXIA provision and the particular provision or instrument said to conflict. Determine whether there is an actual variation or inconsistency. Apply the override only to the extent supported by the text; section 378ZQ preserves non-varied and non-inconsistent provisions.

distinctions.title: Override for inconsistency and general application of private-company provisions
distinctions.left: Section 378ZQ gives Chapter XXIA priority over inconsistent provisions of other laws or instruments.
distinctions.right: Section 378ZR addresses qualified application of private-company provisions to Producer Companies.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 378ZQ as repealing or excluding every other law for Producer Companies.
misconceptions.correction: The section preserves other provisions to the extent they are not varied by, or inconsistent with, Chapter XXIA.

misconceptions.trap: Invoking an override without identifying the actual inconsistent provision.
misconceptions.correction: Identify both the relevant Chapter XXIA text and the competing provision or instrument and explain the inconsistency.

misconceptions.trap: Confusing a conflict rule with a general rule about private-company status.
misconceptions.correction: Use section 378ZQ for inconsistency analysis and section 378ZR for qualified application of private-company provisions.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 378zq do?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The provisions of this Chapter override other laws to the extent of inconsistency, in matters relating to Producer Companies.
